relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n41" value="Incremental by digest.<br><br>Steps 5 and 6 only touch the files whose<br>SHA-1 changed: 156 of 4 208 on the last run.<br><br>Steps 3, 4, 7 and 8 always do the whole<br>corpus — a clone cannot be partial, and a<br>graph cannot be: renaming B changes the<br>edges of every A that imports it, and those<br>A did not change." style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=10;fontColor=#666666;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;spacing=2;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="1220" y="80" width="300" height="200" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n42" value="A run that dies leaves nothing half-written.<br><br>The recovery cursor is captured before the<br>clone and stored only on success, so a failed<br>run never moves it forward and never lets a<br>file be skipped.<br><br>A file entry is written after its chunks, so<br>an interrupted run leaves the older digest<br>and the file is reindexed rather than<br>wrongly considered done." Stored on the<br>chunks, a file cut into twenty pieces carried twenty copies of<br>its history — which is what made a real history unaffordable.<br><br>One point per file also gives a deterministic id, so the API<br>answers "who imports this?" with a retrieve by key rather than<br>a scan of 32 630 points.<br><br>A change of embedding_model or chunking_version recreates<br>kalisio_code and kalisio_code_files together: chunks written<br>under an older contract cannot even be matched for deletion." style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=10;fontColor=#666666;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;spacing=2;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="820" y="540" width="740" height="230" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n12" value="Change detection reads the digests from two places: the chunk payloads (the file has chunks) and the file<br>entries (the file yields none). The chunks win where both know a file — losing the code collection must mean a<br>full reindex, and the file entries survive it." style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=10;fontColor=#666666;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;spacing=2;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="800" width="1520" height="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> <diagram id="built-api-mcp" name="built · API and MCP"> <mxGraphModel dx="1400" dy="800" grid="1" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="1" page="1" pageScale="1" pageWidth="1600" pageHeight="1020" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="n1" value="One FastAPI application. vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="690" width="760" height="210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n7" value="<b>The rest of the /mcp surface</b><br>GET /mcp/ → opens an SSE stream (stateless: carries nothing)<br>PUT /mcp/ → 405, as JSON-RPC<br><br>JSON-RPC methods answered:<br> initialize the handshake, negotiates the version<br> tools/list the two tools and their schemas<br> nothing imports it. A refactor is safe.<br>indexed: false · dependent_count: 0 → the graph cannot speak for this file. Nothing can be concluded.<br><br>Three cases produce the second: no entry at all, an entry written by an ingestion older than the graph, and a<br>file type the graph does not cover (markdown, json). They collapse on purpose — the honest answer is the same.<br>Between deploying the graph and the first nightly run that builds it, every file in the corpus is in that state." style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=10;fontColor=#666666;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;spacing=2;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="930" width="1540" height="180" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> <diagram id="built-graph" name="built · dependency graph"> <mxGraphModel dx="1400" dy="800" grid="1" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="1" page="1" pageScale="1" pageWidth="1600" pageHeight="1000" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="n1" value="ingestion/pipeline/dependency_graph.py — step 7. width="260" height="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n13" value="Never invented<br><br>A specifier that resolves to a file<br>nobody scanned yields no edge at all.<br><br>The prototype did parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="700" y="420" width="560" height="230" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n16" value="Stored on the file entry,<br>not in a fourth collection.<br><br>That point already style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=10;fontColor=#666666;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;spacing=2;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="1300" y="420" width="260" height="230" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n17" value="Rebuilt whole on every run — it cannot be incremental<br><br>If B is renamed, the edges of every A that imports it change. Those A did not change, so no incremental<br>selection would ever revisit them.
